profile.campus: Stream Dallas-Fort Worth area (DFWA site, Garland, TX, not the same campus as the separate DFW IV site)
profile.reading: Stream Data Centers DFWA sits at 1813 Lookout Drive in Garland, Texas, one of Stream Dallas-Fort Worth area facilities. Per Stream own site, the 23-acre site carries 43 megawatts of critical capacity across 275,000 square feet, served by a dedicated 95 megawatt Oncor electric substation. Phase 1 was commissioned in January 2020, and the facility was reported fully leased as of 2023 to an unnamed major cloud customer. Stream own Dallas facilities page states no shared-campus relationship between DFWA and the separate DFW IV facility elsewhere in the metro area, which sits in Richardson and was sold by Stream back in 2011, well before DFWA was commissioned, so the two should be understood as unrelated Stream projects in the same broad market rather than phases of one campus. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners, a larger commercial real estate firm. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds announced acquisition of a majority stake in Stream in August 2025 and completed the deal in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. The company markets its wholesale, powered-shell, and build-to-suit data center model, claiming more than 90 percent of its capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers and describing a pipeline exceeding four gigawatts with more than 27 delivered developments across markets including Dallas-Fort Worth, Phoenix, Chicago, San Antonio, and Atlanta. Garland sits in the eastern Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, a submarket that has drawn substantial hyperscale investment in recent years thanks to available land, strong Oncor grid capacity, and proximity to the broader Dallas fiber and interconnection ecosystem centered around older facilities like the Infomart, factors consistent with Stream decision to secure a dedicated 95 megawatt substation for this specific site.
profile.research_note: 43 MW / 275,000 sqft / 23-acre site / 95MW Oncor substation / Jan 2020 Phase 1 commissioning sourced to Stream own Dallas facilities page. Explicitly noted DFWA and DFW IV are not the same campus, since both are in this operator dataset and could otherwise be confused. Company background from Stream own history/news pages.

reading.body:
Stream Data Centers DFWA is a 43-megawatt facility in Garland, Texas, commissioned in January 2020 across 275,000 square feet on a 23-acre site. The operator's published specifications show the site backed by a dedicated 95-megawatt Oncor electric substation. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, typical for AI training clusters, the 43 megawatts of IT capacity translates to roughly 1,075 racks. The site was reported fully leased as of 2023 to an unnamed major cloud customer.

DFWA ranks outside the top 18 published-capacity facilities in Texas by operator disclosure, placing it at number 19 among the 133 facilities mapped in the state. Texas has published capacity totaling 468 megawatts across all disclosed sites. This campus does not appear in certifications or other qualifications published by the operator.

Garland sits in the eastern Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, a submarket that has attracted hyperscale investment due to available land and strong Oncor grid capacity. The dedicated substation capacity of 95 megawatts exceeds current IT load by more than two times, signaling room for future build-out on the site. The facility's full leasing and proximity to the Dallas fiber and interconnection ecosystem suggest it serves established hyperscale demand rather than speculative capacity.
